title: Ten App Servers, One Busy Database
description: After scaling from two to ten stateless instances, API CPU is low but database connection count and write latency soar. Which response follows the measured bottleneck?

options.text: Keep adding instances because capacity is always linear.
options.explanation: Shared state can cap total throughput. More callers and connection pools can increase contention at the same database.

options.text: Move sessions back into each instance's memory.
options.explanation: That breaks interchangeability and does not address the database's connection and write pressure.

options.text: Add a CDN to distribute database commits.
options.explanation: A CDN can offload cacheable reads and bytes, not commit authoritative database writes.

options.text: Cap app scaling, pool connections and tune or scale the measured stateful write path.
options.explanation: Horizontal app scaling moved the bottleneck to shared state. Protect connection limits and investigate cheaper writes, batching or partitioning as justified by measurements.
